study type: Cohort study (data from a randomized controlled trial)
exposure: maternal early pregnancy BMI classification (underweight, normal weight, overweight/obese)
cohort: The study analyzed data from 1273 women enrolled in the Complex Lipids in Mothers and Babies (CLIMB) randomized controlled trial in Chongqing, China, and their 1017 children who participated in neurocognitive development follow-up.
finding: Abnormal early pregnancy BMI was associated with increased risks of adverse pregnancy outcomes in Chinese women, while early pregnancy BMI had no significant influence on infant neurocognitive development at 12 months of age.
mod_finding: Overweight/obese BMI was associated with an increased risk of caesarean section.
